sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Log outputs setup
sections.what: Removes the default output and adds two destinations: the console, showing info and above, and a daily log file that keeps 30 days and records debug detail.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets developers watch progress live and review problems later.
sections.watch_out: The file path is relative to where the program starts, so logs can end up in a different folder depending on the start location.

sections.name: get_logger
sections.title: Named logger helper
sections.what: Returns a logger tagged with the name of the module that asks for it, so each message shows where it came from.
sections.why: Makes it easy to see which part of the app wrote a message.

summary: Sets up how the app writes its log messages, to the screen and to daily files.
purpose: Lets developers watch the app live and look back at problems later.
why: Likely reason: the console shows progress while the file keeps a record for debugging.
how: Removes the default output, adds a console output showing info and above, and adds a daily file under a logs folder that keeps 30 days and records debug detail. get_logger tags each message with the module name.
inputs: Log calls from the rest of the app.
outputs: Console lines and daily log files in the logs folder.
risks: The log file path is relative to the folder the program is started from, so logs can land in different places. The logs folder must exist or be created by the logger.
debug: If no log file appears, check the working directory of the program and the logs folder. If messages are missing, check the level set for each output.
